name: Morelight
examine: Chief of Staff. Tall, tireless, and extremely proud of the mustache.
lines: President. Morelight, Chief of Staff. The mustache and I are at your service.
If you're ever lost, follow the yellow arrow. If the arrow is lost, come and find me.
You've seen it now, President. The world out there.
The Chamber works both ways, and the Chamber Key works any time. I commute now. It's lovely.
Still here. Still ours. But the gates aren't the edge of the world anymore.
Everything's ready, President. The Coordinates, the Power Cell, the Permit, the press. Even the blueprints, the Contractor says.
Once we switch that Chamber on, we go where Expedition One meant to go. Somewhere nobody has been since the Lockdown. Are you sure?
Then let's go. Carefully. And with snacks.
Take all the time you need. The walls aren't going anywhere. That's the problem.
First, the people. Read the Signed Press Release to the Reporter by the podiums. Use it on her.
Nobody should wake up to find their President gone without a word.
The Contractor says the bunker dig turned up old blueprints. For the Chamber. Ask him for them.
The Chamber is at the far north end of the Trenches, past Captain Motion's barricade.
Use each part on it: the blueprints, the Coordinates Drive, the Power Cell, the Exit Permit. Then feed it 20 Scrap Hash.
When the doors open, step through. I'll be right behind you.
The doors are open? Then go, President. I'll be right behind you. Probably.
The last barricade, President. And Captain Motion.
The same. He led them north on day one. Whatever he found up there, he never came back to report it.
He's guarded that last barricade ever since. Running.
In circles. Very fast circles. The Scout knows him better than anyone. Talk to the Scout first.
The Captain hits fast but tires. Stand your ground and keep your health up.
And President? Wear your best armor. And bring him down gently if you can. He was one of ours.

lines.player: He stopped. He said the Chamber's dead, and he kept running so nobody would see.

lines: ...A year of laps, to hide a broken machine. Poor man.
But dead isn't gone, President. The Scout's been up to look. The Chamber is whole. It's just asleep.
Expedition One had the courage. What they didn't have was the parts.
Coordinates, from the Sysadmin's lost files. A Power Cell, which the Party Planner's gala could pay for.
An Exit Permit, which only the Broker can sign; the Fixer knows him. And the public on our side, which is the Spin Doctor's department.
Bring me all four, and we finish what Expedition One started.
The Chief has gone quiet. For the first time in recorded history, a Wrong-Namer has stopped talking.
I had a plaque made. It says 'It's $BITCOIN.' You can hang it in the bunker.
The last barricade. And the man in front of it. Rest up, then come and see me.
President, the Wrong-Namers. They've dug in past the first barricade.
People who decided the walls are a comfort. There is no outside, they say. It's all a con. $BITCON, they call our coin.
They turn back anyone heading north. Shouting, mostly. Megaphones, occasionally.
Start with a Heckler. Then knock over a Sockpuppet; that brings out their Chief at the second barricade.
Correct them, President. Firmly. With whatever you're holding.
One Heckler down! Now the Sockpuppets. They hide behind cardboard and agree with each other.
Knock one over and the whole act falls apart.
The Chief guards the second barricade. He calls for Sockpuppets when he's losing, so finish him fast.
Melee beats shields. Guns, less so. Trust the triangle, President.
The Sludge Mother is gone? Splendid. I'll have the Trenches hosed down. Twice.
And President, the Scout sent word. Expedition One's Captain is still up there, past the barricades.
Still running, apparently. Which is more than any of us expected.
The next stretch belongs to the Wrong-Namers. Catch your breath and come back to me.
You made it through training in one piece. The mustache and I are proud.
Now, the real job. The north end of the wall is the only stretch nobody has checked since the Lockdown.
Because the only way there is the Trenches. On the first day of the Lockdown, twelve brave fools called Expedition One dug them, heading north.
Nobody came back up to tell us. And since then, something has clogged the Trenches. Our people call it the Sludge Mother.
The Scout keeps a camp just inside the entrance. The Scout was there on day one. Start there.
The Mother calls her little ones when she's hurt. Hit hard and keep moving.
Bring Talking Points. Lots of them. Sludge is very hard to get out of a suit.
Welcome back, President. Finish what you're doing and come and see me. We have walls to get past.
Ah, President! Morelight, your Chief of Staff. Welcome to your first day in office.

lines.player: Where is everyone? And why is the treasury... empty?

lines: A small accounting incident. The Treasurer bought the wrong coin. With all of it.
The ticker crashed, and the gates sealed themselves. We call it the Lockdown. Nobody has left the Treasury since.
Not yet. I have a plan for that. But first, the basics: Mining, Fundraising, Lobbying. You can't escape on an empty stomach.
See The Treasurer in the main hall, just north. Follow the yellow arrow. It has never steered me wrong.
Come back to me whenever you're lost. I'll be right here, guarding the mustache.
The Treasurer gave you the petty cash? Good. Don't spend it on snacks.
Now make some real money. The Sysadmin looks after the old server racks on the east lawn.
Mine some Hash, then sell it at the Trading Terminal in the hall. It pays in $BITCOIN at today's price.
Check the ticker in the corner. It changes. Constantly. That's half the fun and all of the stress.
Money in your pocket and Hash on your shoes. Now, self-defense.
The Drill Sergeant runs the training yard to the south-west. Spam Bots, Sludgelings, Comment Trolls. All very beatable.

lines.player: Do I really need to fight?

lines: Out there? Constantly. In here? Only things that say 'gm' forty times a minute.
Buy a Campaign Pistol at the Terminal, wield it and clear the yard. Then try your gavel. A President should know both.
You fight like a natural. Now, let's talk about donors.
The Party Planner hosts dinners in the west garden. Work the room and you'll dig up scandals.
Take them to The Spin Doctor's podium and spin them into Talking Points. Recite one when you're hurt.
You're a politician. Talking is the only thing that has ever healed one.
Next, the lobbyists. Someone has to hand them business cards, and it can't be me. I'm far too tall to be discreet.
The Fixer lurks on the east lawn. Do favors for the lobbyists and they'll pay you. Usually.
Sometimes they find photos. Then the favor is free. Keep your photos boring, President.
Every President needs a security detail. Ours is... small. And blue.
The Sproto Handler in the main hall has a contract for you. Summon a Sproto and it fights at your side.
Perfectly. As long as you never call them gremlins. They hate that.
You're carrying half the lawn. Use a Bank Booth in the main hall and deposit what you don't need.
The bank holds four hundred stacks. I've seen Presidents fill it with Scrap Hash. Don't be that President.
One more thing. Every leader needs somewhere to hide when the ticker goes red.
The Contractor in the main hall can build you a bunker. Go and ask about it.
You've learned everything I can teach you in a garden. Time for the real thing.
The Trenches run north from the south-east lawn. Somewhere past the far end is the only part of the wall nobody's checked.
Step inside and your training is done. Then come back to me. I'll have work for you.
The kind that gets us out of here.

name: The Treasurer
examine: Bought the wrong coin. Feels terrible about it.
lines: ATTENTION ATTENTION! Oh. President. Sorry. Habit.
About the national reserve... I may have misread the ticker. Slightly. Completely.
We bought $BITCOIN. The People's Bitcoin. One billion of them. Not the other one. The ticker crashed, and the gates sealed: the Lockdown.
We can't sell, and we can't leave, so we earn. Mine, fundraise, lobby, and sell what we make at the Trading Terminal in this hall.
Here's what's left of the petty cash. Please spend it wisely. Please.
President! The reserve is less empty. I only checked the ticker eleven times today.
The Terminal pays whatever the ticker says. Sell your Hash when it's green, buy your gear when it's red.

lines.player: Any more accounting incidents I should know about?

lines: None! Er. Well. The Lockdown. But that one is technically a security incident.

name: The Sysadmin
examine: Has not seen daylight since the last fiscal year.
lines: Oh, hi. Don't touch the blinking ones. Actually, do. That's how mining works.
These racks still mine Hash. Take my spare pick. It's rusty, but so am I.

lines.player: What do I do with Hash?

lines: Sell it at the Terminal. Or load it into a Hash Cannon, if you like explosions. I like explosions.
Inventory full? Bank it or sell it. Better picks from the Terminal mine faster.
You did it. The racks are cool, the Rogue Process is gone, and OUTSIDE.TXT is safe.
Take the Coordinates Drive to Morelight. Whatever's out there, it has an address.
And keep the Overclocked Pick. It runs hot. Like me, after that fight.
Bad news. The liquid-cooled racks in the west wing are cooking themselves, and something on the network is fighting me.
It's guarding a file. OUTSIDE.TXT. From before the Lockdown. Nobody's opened it in years.
First, coolant. Fill this canister at the Gremlin Fountain. That water has never frozen and never boiled. Use the canister on the statue.
Then use the coolant on a Liquid-Cooled Rack in the west wing.
If anything asks for my password, it's my cat's name. Lord Fluffington the Third. Don't tell anyone.
That red window! A Rogue Process. It's loose in the west wing, guarding OUTSIDE.TXT. Shut it down, President!
It's down! Now I just need the admin password to recover the file. Which was it? You heard me say it.
No, that's the Treasurer's. Think, President.
YES. Logging in... recovering OUTSIDE.TXT...
It's coordinates. Coordinates to somewhere that isn't here.
That's what the Wrong-Namers chant. Never type that in here.
Back for more Hash? Respect.
Humming racks need Mining 15. The liquid-cooled racks inside the hall need Mining 30.
A Steel Pick works from Mining 15, a Quantum Pick from 35. Both on the Terminal. Tell them I sent you. They won't care.

name: The Party Planner
examine: Knows every donor and every dessert.
lines: Darling! You must be the President. Love the suit. Hate the treasury.
Donors adore a dinner. Work the room and you'll overhear all sorts of scandals.
Here's a Donor List. The fancier the dinner, the better the list you'll need.

lines.player: And what do I do with scandals?

lines: Take them to The Spin Doctor. A raw scandal is useless. A spun one is practically a meal.
Oh, and every so often a whale pledges a fortune. Smile and nod, darling. Smile and nod.
Darling, the disco ball is still spinning. The Power Cell is yours. Whatever Morelight's building, it had better have a dance floor.
Darling, the masks were a triumph. Nobody knew who anybody was. The Power Cell is yours; Morelight says it's for 'a door'.
Darling, a garden party under a sealed sky. Poetic. The Power Cell is yours. Go and find a real sky.
Darling! The gala of the year. Morelight needs a Power Cell for some 'little project', and power cells are not cheap.
So we throw a party, the donors pay, and you, President, are the host. First things first: the theme.
Masks! Mystery! Nobody will recognize the Treasurer. Perfect.
A disco ball! I already own four. Wonderful.
Outdoors, under a sealed sky. Bold. I love it.
Catering! Bring me 5 Minor Scandals for the gossip table and 3 Soundbites for the toasts.
A gala without gossip is just dinner, darling.
CRASHERS! Party Crashers in my garden! And one of them stole the guest list!
Throw them out, President. Firmly. Bring me back that list.
You have the list? Give it here, darling, before anyone else 'borrows' it.
Darling! The donors still talk about your first dinner. Mostly the chicken.
At Fundraising 20 you can work the Gala Dinner. At 40, the Yacht Party. Bring a Rolodex, or better, a Black Book.
Juicier scandals spin into better Talking Points. Everyone wins. Except the press.

name: The Spin Doctor
examine: Can make anything sound like good news.
lines: Ah, a patient! I mean a client. I mean... the President.
A raw scandal is useless. Bring it to my podium and spin it into a Talking Point.

lines.player: What does a Talking Point do?

lines: Recite one in a fight and you feel better. It's science. Political science.
Spin badly and the story blows up in your face. Practice, President. Practice.
Front page, President! 'A DOOR FOR EVERYONE.' I couldn't have written it better. I tried.
Take the Teleprompter. Read it and you're home. And keep that press release for when you need the people.
If the President vanishes, the Treasury will panic. If the President explains, the Treasury will cheer.
So: a press conference. The Reporter is waiting by the podiums. But first, practice.
Bring me 3 Soundbites. We'll warm up your voice.
The Reporter is by the podiums. Remember: never confirm, never deny, always pivot.
Optimism, President. Always optimism.
Well? How did it go? ...Come, sit. Tell me everything.
My star pupil! Your Soundbites are trending.
Juicy scandals become Zingers at Spin 20. Mega scandals become Mic Drops at 40.
Practice enough and nothing ever blows up in your face. Mostly.

name: The Fixer
examine: Knows a guy. Is the guy.
lines: ...You didn't see me. I'm not here. These cards aren't here either. Take them.
Lobbyists pay for favors. Hand out cards, shake hands, get paid in $BITCOIN.
Completely. Mostly. Sometimes they find photos. Then the favor's free and you smile anyway.
Bigger lobbyists pay better, if your Lobbying is up to it. Now walk away slowly.
You burned them. Clean hands. The Broker signed anyway; he respects that. I think it scared him.
You used them. The Broker signed so fast he broke the pen. Remind me never to get on your bad side.
...You want out. Everyone wants out. The Lockdown Act says nobody leaves without an Exit Permit.
Only the Broker can stamp one. He wants this envelope delivered first. Don't open it.
He stands by the lobbyists on the east lawn. Use the envelope on him.
A photo of you? Classic Broker. Someone took that photo, and they have the negatives.
Word is he paid the Paper-Hands goblins in the Trenches. They never hold anything for long. Go and take it off them.
You got the negatives. Now you've got options.
Clean. The Broker will sign; he won't want a fight. Here's your permit, and something for your trouble.
Ruthless. He'll sign, and he'll pay. Here's your permit. Don't spend it all at once.
You again. Good. The lobbyists like you.
Veteran lobbyists pay better from Lobbying 20. The Brokers want 40, and they only take Platinum Cards.
Keep your photos boring, President. Blackmail is bad for business.

name: The Drill Sergeant
lines: LISTEN UP, PRESIDENT! You are soft! You are slow! You are, frankly, very well dressed!
Buy a gun at the Terminal! Every gun takes the same Rounds! Here's a stack, on the house!
Cannons fire the Hash you mine and blow up everything around the target! I LOVE CANNONS!
Pick a style in the Equipment tab: Accurate, Rapid or Longrange! Take the gun off and you swing your gavel! That's Melee!
Start on the Spam Bots, then the Sludgelings, then the Comment Trolls! DISMISSED!
AT EASE, PRESIDENT! You passed basic!
The Trenches are through the entrance on the south-east lawn! Every barricade has a boss in front of it!
Rounds run out fast! Buy them by the hundred and pack Talking Points to heal! NOW GIVE ME TWENTY!
Twenty Scrap Hash! For the budget! DISMISSED!

name: The Sproto Handler
examine: Covered in tiny bite marks. Proud of every one.
lines: Careful, they bite. Only the ones who don't like you. So, careful.
Sprotos are little soldiers who fight beside you. Use a contract to summon one.
Loyal, blue and extremely brave. Do NOT call them gremlins.
One at a time. Specials cost Summoning points; check the Summoning tab. Here's a Recruit contract.
Your Recruit won't stop talking about you. Well. Squeaking.
Medics at Summoning 10, Grunts at 20, Snipers at 30, Heavies at 45. Contracts are on the Terminal.
Watch your Summoning points. A special at the right moment wins fights.

name: The Contractor
examine: Has a pencil behind each ear.
lines: Every President needs a bunker. Somewhere to hide when the ticker goes red.
Right under this hall. I'll need materials: 10 Scrap Hash and 2 Soundbites.
Morale. My crew won't dig without a good speech. Bring both and the hatch is yours.
Blueprints? For the Chamber? I found these while digging your bunker. Thought they were a pizza menu.
Here. Take them to the Chamber and follow along. Don't touch the red lever. Or do. I'm not your boss.
The hatch is yours, President. Climb down any time.
Build spots are marked down there. Click one to see what you can build.
Bigger builds need a Pro or Elite Toolkit, plus Concrete, Steel Beams and Circuit Boards from the Terminal.
Old papers. Drawings of some big machine. Probably nothing. I'll hang on to them.

name: The Scout
examine: Lookout for Expedition One. Has been in the Trenches longer than the Trenches.
lines: Welcome to the Trenches. Mind the craters.
The Scout. I was the lookout for Expedition One.
Twelve of us went north on the first day of the Lockdown. I'm the one who came back down.
Went home. Gave up. Got lost. One of them is still up there, if you listen at night.
We dug them along the inside of the wall, heading for the north end. Took us a week.
Since then the Treasury's been tipping its worst down here. Panic. Doubt. People who sell at the first sign of trouble.
It gets nastier the further north you go. Each barricade opens once you beat whatever stands in front of it.
The old maps call it a Teleport Chamber. Out of service.
I heard it hum once. Just once. That's why I'm still here.
If you fall, your pack stays where you dropped. Come back for it quick.
And Talking Points. Never leave the Treasury without them.
I heard it from all the way down here. The hum. Then a big bang. Then nothing.
You made it out. Expedition One made it out. Took us long enough.
Soon. Somebody has to walk the Captain through. He's not used to going slowly.
Morelight's really doing it? Waking the Chamber?
Go on up. I'll keep the Trenches quiet behind you. The Captain's sitting by the Chamber already. Wouldn't miss it.
You stopped him. I heard it. The running. It stopped.
He's sitting by the Chamber now, catching his breath. Says he'll be first in line if it ever wakes up.
Tell Morelight what he told you. And President... thank you.
So it's the Captain's turn.
He was our leader. Best runner in the Treasury. We reached the north end in a week, and there it was: the Chamber. Cold. Dead.
The Captain wouldn't accept it. 'Keep moving,' he said. 'Momentum is everything.' He's been running laps in front of it ever since.
So nobody else sees it doesn't work. So nobody else gives up. I think that's what he tells himself.
He moves twice as fast as anyone. Don't chase him. Let him come to you.
Then stop him, President. Gently, if you can. Then let's bring him home.
Quiet up there. Quieter than it's been in a year. Thank you.
Only the Captain left now. Morelight will want to talk to you about him.
Wrong-Namers everywhere past the first barricade. My ears are still ringing.
They weren't always like this. Some of them were Treasury clerks. Got scared of the walls, then got more scared of what's past them.
Their Chief guards the second barricade. Bring a hammer. Shields hate hammers.
The first barricade's open. First time in four hundred days. I counted.
Past it, the Wrong-Namers. They'll tell you there's nothing out there. Don't listen.
Morelight sent you? Good. I was running out of patience and snacks.
Twelve of us dug these Trenches. Then the panic of the Lockdown came down after us and pooled up. That's her. The Sludge Mother.
She squats at the first barricade, straight north. When she's hurt she calls up Sludgelings.
Clear the little ones if they swarm you, then go back to Mom. And don't step in anything.
More Trenches. And past those, the Captain. Still running. I can hear him some nights.

name: The Reporter
lines: Treasury Times, live. No comment? Everyone has a comment.
Since the Lockdown, the news is the only thing that gets in or out.
President! Any plans to leave the Treasury? ...Off the record?

lines.player: Off the record: watch the north end of the Trenches.

lines: I KNEW it. I'll keep it quiet. Mostly.
President! Big news? Hand it over. Use the press release on me and I'll read it live.
We're live! President, first question: is it true the Treasury bought the wrong coin?
Honesty! In politics! I need to sit down.
(Somewhere, the Spin Doctor faints. Try again.)

options.text: We bought the RIGHT coin. Everyone else bought the wrong one.
lines: ...That's going on the front page. Next question!
I'll... print that, I guess. Let's try again.
Second question: why can't the Treasury just sell its $BITCOIN?
Ouch. That's a headline you don't want. Try again.

options.text: Because we took the Never Sell Vow. We're builders.
lines: Builders! The people love builders. Last question!

options.text: Because the sell button is broken.
lines: Is it? ...It is, isn't it. Try again.
Final question: rumor says you're planning to leave the Treasury. Is that true?
'No comment' is a comment, President. Try again.
Noted. Bitterly. Try again.

options.text: Leave? I'm opening a door. For everyone.
lines: A door for everyone. The Treasury is going to love that. That's a wrap!
That's a wrap. You were... surprisingly good. Go see your Spin Doctor.

name: Morelight
examine: Chief of Staff. Somehow already here.
lines: ...We made it. Look at that, President. No walls.
Somewhere new. The coordinates only got us this far. Everything past that hill is unexplored.
The Chamber works both ways. Go home whenever you like; the Treasury will want to hear about this.
I'm going to stand here a while. Guarding the mustache. From a much better view.
